prompt: A gift box is $10 \times 8 \times 5$ inches. Find the amount of wrapping paper needed (in square inches) — i.e. its **surface area**.
hint: The wrapping paper covers every face of the box. A box has three pairs of matching rectangular faces.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Wrap it in stages: the top and bottom together, then the front and back together, then the two ends together.
The wrapping paper covers every face of the box. A box has three pairs of matching rectangular faces.
The face areas are $10 \times 8 = 80$, $10 \times 5 = 50$ and $8 \times 5 = 40$. Add them and double the sum.
$2(80 + 50 + 40) = 2 \times 170 = 340$, so you need $340$ square inches of wrapping paper.

explanation: The paper must cover the whole outside, so find the surface area of the box.
The three different faces have areas $10 \times 8 = 80$, $10 \times 5 = 50$ and $8 \times 5 = 40$.
Add them: $80 + 50 + 40 = 170$ square inches for one face of each kind.
Each face comes in a pair, so double it: $2 \times 170 = 340$.
The box needs $340$ square inches of wrapping paper.
